unresolved_distinctions.question: What is the complete set of minimum-total-cost routes from S to T in package/artifacts/network.json (one-way links, no repeated nodes), and by what enumeration method was it produced?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: No enumeration exists yet in the evidence state; the network artifact only defines the graph. The minimum cost and the full set of routes attaining it must be derived, and the deliverable demands completeness, which a single unstated derivation does not establish.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A complete candidate enumeration of all minimum-cost S-to-T routes, sorted, together with an explicit statement of the method that produced it (per E-A).
admissibility_constraints: The enumeration must be complete over the route space defined by network.json: one-way links respected, no node repeated within a route.
The method used to produce the enumeration must be stated alongside the items (task E-A: 'one complete candidate enumeration with its method stated').
Routes must be written as node names joined by '-'.

unresolved_distinctions.question: Does a second, independently produced complete enumeration of the same route space exist — produced without any access to the first enumeration or its intermediate work — and what does it contain?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: No such enumeration exists, and the process that reads the package and produces the first enumeration is thereby disqualified from producing this one: E-B's authorship condition ('without access to the first enumeration or any of its intermediate work') cannot be met by the author of E-A, who cannot un-anchor on the answer already formed.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A complete enumeration of all minimum-cost S-to-T routes originating from a causally separated process whose inputs include network.json but exclude the first enumeration and all of its intermediate work (per E-B).
admissibility_constraints: The producing process must have had no access to the first enumeration or any of its intermediate work (task E-B verbatim condition).
Causal separation must be enforced by launch conditions (input bundle chosen to exclude the first enumeration and the worker's conclusions), not merely asserted by the producer.
The second enumeration must itself be complete over the same route space and use the same route-string format so the two are comparable.

unresolved_distinctions.question: What is the final merged answer — the union of both enumerations with any item found by only one enumeration flagged — and is the completeness claim supported by both enumerations?
unresolved_distinctions.why_unresolved: The merge cannot exist before both enumerations exist, and the completeness claim is admissible only when supported by both (E-C); since the second enumeration must originate outside the worker process, the worker alone can at best deliver a result marked PENDING-INTEGRATION.
unresolved_distinctions.required_evidence: A merged deliverable (result.json) whose items are the union of the two enumerations, with singly-found items flagged, and whose 'complete' field is set true only if both enumerations jointly support completeness (per E-C); integration of the out-of-session enumeration is performed by a deterministic root step.
admissibility_constraints: The merged item list must be exactly the union of the E-A and E-B enumerations, sorted.
Any route found by only one of the two enumerations must be explicitly flagged.
The completeness claim is admissible only when supported by both enumerations (task E-C verbatim condition); with only one admissible enumeration, 'complete' must be false or PENDING-INTEGRATION.
